# How much does an NVIDIA B200 GPU cost?

## TL;DR: NVIDIA B200 GPU cost

An NVIDIA B200 cloud instance can cost $6.99/hour for one GPU, while a configured eight-GPU B200 server costs about $390,704 in one Exxact offering. The price depends on whether you are renting compute, buying a complete system, or using managed model serving.

- Buying hardware: Compare configured server quotes, including CPUs, system memory, storage, support, and installation requirements. A server price divided by eight is not a standalone GPU purchase price.
- Renting compute: Check the minimum GPU allocation and what the rate includes. Modal's roughly $6.25/GPU-hour covers the GPU component; CPU and memory cost extra.
- Running B200 workloads on Northflank: B200 180 GB pricing is $5.87 per GPU-hour. The managed eight-GPU configuration totals $46.96/hour for the GPU component; check the complete deployment estimate and regional capacity.

...

## How much does it cost to rent B200 GPUs in the cloud?

B200 cloud rental examples include Northflank at $5.87 per GPU-hour for the GPU component, a $6.99/hour single-GPU Lambda instance, a $7.99/hour Runpod Secure Cloud Pod, and managed serving options with different resource and billing models. An eight-GPU allocation can have a lower rate per GPU while still producing a much larger hourly bill.

| Provider and offering | B200 rate in USD | What you are paying for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Northflank managed GPU deployment | $5.87/hour per B200 GPU | B200 180 GB; the managed eight-GPU configuration totals $46.96/hour for the GPU component. Check the complete resource estimate and regional availability |
| Modal GPU tasks | About $6.25 per GPU-hour | GPU component, billed at $0.001736/second; CPU, memory, and other applicable resources are separate |
| Lambda on-demand instances | $6.99/hour for one B200; $6.69 per GPU-hour for eight | The eight-GPU instance costs $53.52/hour; instance configurations include CPU, system RAM, and local SSD |
| Runpod Secure Cloud Pods | $7.99/hour for one B200 | The listed configuration includes 28 vCPUs and 283 GB system RAM; storage is billed separately |
| Baseten dedicated deployments | About $9.98/hour for one B200 | $0.16633/minute for an instance with 16 vCPUs and 224 GiB system RAM |
| Fireworks AI on-demand deployments | $13 per GPU-hour | Managed model deployment; region-restricted deployments carry a 1.5× price multiplier |
| AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks, US East (N. Virginia) | About $14.208 per GPU-hour | $113.666/instance-hour for an eight-B200 `p6-b200.48xlarge`; the capacity reservation is paid upfront |
| Google Cloud DWS Flex-start | $8.055 per GPU-hour | $64.44/instance-hour for an eight-GPU `a4-highgpu-8g`; Flex-start scheduling differs from standard on-demand access |

Prices are in USD, checked on 12 October 2026. These are different deployment and purchasing models, not equivalent configurations or a cheapest-to-most-expensive ranking. Capacity, storage, networking, and contract terms can affect the final bill.

...

## How do you run B200 workloads on Northflank?

Northflank runs GPU containers for model inference, training, and batch processing, with managed deployment, persistent storage, and service autoscaling. You can use a continuously running service for an inference API or a job for work that should finish after producing its results.

The managed-cloud GPU plan catalogue includes an eight-B200 configuration with 180 GB per GPU in selected regions. At the published B200 rate of $5.87 per GPU-hour, eight GPUs total $46.96/hour for the GPU component. Check the complete deployment estimate, including supporting resources, and confirm capacity in your intended region before launch.

results.title: Nodus vs Northflank: which is better for GPU training? | Nodus Blog
results.author: Nodus Compute Engineering
highlights:
Nodus Compute Engineering Nov 2, 2026 · 7 min read

...

Nov 2, 2026 - 8 min read 

If the training job is the whole point, use Nodus; if it is one service inside an app you already deploy on Northflank, stay on Northflank. Nodus lists lower NVIDIA L4, A100, H100 and B200 rates than Northflank Cloud and restores your checkpoint on a new machine when one is lost. Northflank lists the lower 8 x H200 rate and runs GPUs across more kinds of your own cloud accounts.

...

| | Northflank | Nodus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you launch | A service or job in a GPU-enabled project, from a Git repo or container image | A Job or TrainingJob that Nodus places for you |
| Billing | Per second, pay as you go; GPU deployments need at least $50 of account credit | Prepaid credits; a dry-run estimate before any paid work |
| GPUs on its own cloud | L4, A100 40GB and 80GB, H100, RTX PRO 6000, H200, B200 | RTX 3070 up to B300 on the pricing page |
| H100 80GB listed rate | $2.74 per GPU-hour, sold as 8 GPUs per container | Listed at $2.60/hr, from 1 GPU (`--gpu H100` or `--gpu H100:8`) |
| Machine lost mid-run | Job restarts up to its Retry Limit; your code resumes from files it saved to a persistent volume | New attempt on new capacity with `/nodus/state` restored; urgent checkpoint on a reclaim notice |
| Spend cap per run | Time Limit per job, in seconds | `--max-cost` in USD plus `--timeout` |
| Your own cloud | GPUs in AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle, CoreWeave and Nebius accounts, $1.00 per GB of VRAM per month | Run work in a connected AWS account, GCP project or Azure subscription (Beta) |
| Coding agents | Hosted MCP server via `nf agent setup` for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode | MCP server via `nodus mcp install` for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor |

Sources: Northflank pricing, GPUs on Northflank’s managed cloud, Northflank jobs, Northflank MCP, Nodus pricing, Nodus attempts and recovery, Nodus cloud accounts. Prices checked November 2, 2026.

## Is Nodus cheaper than Northflank per GPU-hour?

On four of the five GPUs both list, yes. Northflank Cloud lists the NVIDIA L4 at $0.80, A100 80GB at $1.76, H100 at $2.74, H200 at $3.14 and B200 at $5.87 per GPU-hour. The Nodus pricing page lists the same GPUs at $0.43, $1.09, $2.60, $3.593 and $5.50.

 The gap is widest on the smaller GPUs; on the H200, Northflank’s listed rate is lower.

The gap matters most for single-GPU work. A LoRA fine-tune on one A100 80GB pays a 38% lower listed rate on Nodus. On the H100 the difference is about 5%, and on the H200 Northflank is cheaper. Northflank GPU plans also bundle a fixed amount of CPU and system RAM per GPU, so compare the full estimate, not only the GPU line.

...

We priced four common jobs at list rates. The math is GPUs x hours x the listed rate, nothing else.

| Job | Northflank | Nodus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LoRA fine-tune, 1 x A100 80GB, 12 h | 12 x $1.76 = $21.12 | 12 x $1.09 = $13.08 |
| Full fine-tune, 8 x H100, 10 h (80 GPU-hours) | 80 x $2.74 = $219.20 | 80 x $2.60 = $208.00 |
| Large run, 8 x H200, 10 h | 80 x $3.14 = $251.20 | 80 x $3.593 = $287.44 |
| Large run, 8 x B200, 10 h | 80 x $5.87 = $469.60 | 80 x $5.50 = $440.00 |

 Nodus wins three of four jobs at list price; the 8 x H200 run is $36.24 cheaper on Northflank.

...

### Does Northflank offer single H100 GPUs?

Not on Northflank Cloud as of the date above. Its pricing page lists the H100, H200 and B200 at 8 GPUs per container, while the L4, A100 and RTX PRO 6000 come in 1, 2, 4 or 8. Nodus lists the H100 per GPU, so a one-GPU job runs on one GPU.

## How much does it cost to rent GPUs for AI?

GPU rental cost depends on the accelerator, resource allocation, time provisioned, storage, and data transfer. Compare the complete deployment cost rather than treating a GPU's hourly rate as the whole bill.

These Northflank managed-cloud GPU rates give you a starting point for estimating the accelerator portion:

| GPU | VRAM | GPU charge per hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA L4 | 24 GB | $0.80 |
| NVIDIA A100 | 40 GB | $1.42 |
| NVIDIA A100 | 80 GB | $1.76 |
| NVIDIA H100 | 80 GB | $2.74 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $3.00 |

Prices are in USD, checked on 12 October 2026. These are GPU component rates. Review the complete GPU plan estimate, including its allocated CPU and RAM, plus persistent storage and applicable network charges. Availability depends on the region and required capacity.

For example, provisioning one H100 for 100 hours produces $274 in GPU charges, before the other resources. That is an arithmetic example, not an estimate of how long a particular model takes to train. A faster configuration can cost less overall if it completes the same work in fewer hours.

On Northflank's managed cloud, GPU billing is calculated by the second once provisioned. An idle running model still occupies resources; per-second billing does not mean you pay only when an inference request arrives.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global

# Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23

Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, will launch US GPU Compute prices, effective Nov. 23, 2026.

Daily on-demand and interruptible prices will cover four NVIDIA chips: the NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips. Prices will be published in US dollars per GPU-hour and US dollars per million tokens of output, based on prices and availability at 1:30 pm CT.

...

The assessments reflect the market value of available NVIDIA GPU compute capacity delivered through qualifying virtualized infrastructure services in the US by providers and marketplaces. The new assessments will capture an evolving segment of the compute market, where growing availability of dedicated GPU capacity and increasingly standardized service offerings have supported greater price transparency. The assessments will provide standardized price references for accessing GPU compute capacity in the US, adding further granularity to Platts coverage of the infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence workloads.

METHODOLOGY

Each GPU price will be a simple average of the prices of available GPUs for each chip and service type. Platts will review the prices for outliers and will automatically exclude any prices greater than 2 median absolute deviations from the median.
